leaf lifespan, and the rate of leaf death, is a function of both nutrient availability and photosynthesis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

leaf lifespan is not a fixed trait, but rather a flexible trait in the context of the whole plant, and that the adaptive significance of the leaf longevity is not restricted to the retranslocation of nutrients, but also includes the ability of the plant to maintain a high rate of carbon gain during leaf ageing.
